questions.question: Which input lists keywords that start with sh at the current prompt?
questions.explanation: A question mark immediately after a partial token requests completions for that token.

questions.question: What does Tab do after a uniquely recognized partial IOS keyword?
questions.explanation: Tab expands an unambiguous keyword without submitting the command.

questions.question: Which key typically recalls the previous IOS CLI command?
questions.explanation: Up arrow moves toward older history entries.

questions.question: You entered show ip followed by a space. Which key lists valid next tokens?
questions.explanation: After a space, ? lists arguments or keywords valid at that position.

questions.question: When can an IOS keyword be shortened?

options.B: Only if it has no arguments
options.C: Whenever it is at least two characters long
options.D: When the leading characters uniquely identify it in that context

questions.explanation: IOS resolves unique prefixes against the valid keywords for the current context.

questions.question: Which IOS editing shortcut moves the cursor to the start of the line?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+A moves to the beginning, while Ctrl+E moves to the end.

questions.question: IOS reports an ambiguous command for a shortened token. What should you do?

options.A: Add identifying letters or inspect possible matches with ?
options.B: Use the same token at a lower privilege level

questions.explanation: An ambiguous token matches multiple keywords in the current context.

questions.question: Illustrative output says % Incomplete command. What is the best next step for a recognized command prefix?

options.B: Append a space and ? to inspect required continuations
options.C: Delete the first character from the command
options.D: Use end to clear interface counters

questions.explanation: The parser recognized the input so far and expects further arguments or keywords.

questions.question: An illustrative IOS error puts a caret under part of your command. What does it mark?

options.A: The approximate position of a dropped packet
options.B: Where the parser detected invalid input
options.C: Where the last saved configuration differs
options.D: The beginning of an interface description

questions.explanation: Inspect the token or command context at the reported parser position.

questions.question: After entering a command and a space, the engineer presses ? and sees <cr> among the choices. What does that entry indicate?

options.A: An argument named cr is required
options.C: The current command can be submitted as entered
options.D: The command must be used in a different mode

questions.explanation: The carriage-return entry means the parser accepts the input without another argument.
